A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ABCD research, despite the changed title. Text, equations, tables and figures support comparison throughout. V1 ends after its references; v3 additionally contains Appendices A–E, which were included in the assessment.

before.justification: V1 reports original MoG experiments and evaluations on Sudoku, Pixel Maze, molecular generation and OGBench, including Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–8.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds experimental outcomes and diagnostic analyses in its appendices, including Tables 3–4 and Figures 9–16.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain cyclic denoising, top-K selection and replication, multiple exploration temperatures, and temperature-origin stopping. V3 explicitly permits zero-noise go-back steps, already represented in v1 Figure 8. Appendix B documents fractional stopping thresholds behind retained experimental curves without establishing an algorithm revision.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same two MoG distributions, Sudoku completion, Pixel Maze generalization, QM9 molecular generation, and OGBench Large/Giant navigation. V3 supplies training-data and task details but does not establish additional dataset or task coverage; its added guidance and temperature conditions concern evaluation settings.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Base Diffusion, BoN, SMC, BS and SoP, while MoG retains fixed go-back alternatives. The new OGBench tables use the same comparator set. Appendix B.3's classifier-guidance discussion describes the base diffusion configuration rather than an additional separately evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix B.7 adds standard-guidance OGBench comparisons alongside the retained Figure 6 results, newly identified as using adaptive guidance. Appendix C.1 adds fixed-temperature evaluation sweeps across three retained tasks. Most other newly stated sample counts, preprocessing choices and budgets document existing experiments rather than establish changed protocols.

E4.justification: V3 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: MoG refinement sequences, OGBench trajectory repair, Sudoku predictions under different noise levels, runtime and iteration allocation by difficulty, and cross-task temperature sensitivity (Figures 9–15). These additions examine search behavior and adaptive computation beyond the retained analyses in Figures 7–8.

E5.justification: V1 already includes uncertainty values in Table 1 and shaded variation in Figure 7(d). V3 newly supplies dispersion values for the retained Sudoku and Pixel Maze benchmark results in Tables 5–6 and explicitly identifies standard deviations in Figures 13–14. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The main plots and MoG Tables 1–2 retain their results. V3 adds substantial standard-guidance OGBench outcomes, including Giant ABCD success of 100 ± 0 at 202.58 seconds with max_iter = 35 (Table 3), plus cross-task temperature findings and qualitative refinement outcomes. Tables 5–7 principally tabulate retained curves; the added OGBench scores do not demonstrate performance changes under the original guidance setting.

T1.justification: V1 contains diffusion preliminaries but no termination theorem. Appendix E in v3 introduces formal stopping-time definitions, bounded-reward, monotonic-selection and attainment assumptions, a claimed finite-time ATT termination theorem, and lemmas and proofs concerning hit probabilities, optimality and finite-time hitting.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive inference-time scaling, the three ABCD components, and improved solution quality and computational efficiency across the same domains. The appendix additions do not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendices B.7.1 and B.9.1 add concrete mechanism interpretations: initial plans can contain invalid segments that cyclic refinement repairs, while unsuitable Sudoku noise levels either freeze errors or overwrite correct predictions. These refine the existing exploration–exploitation explanation. Section 6's scalability limitations and proposed future directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B substantially improves technical disclosure through PyTorch and RTX 4090 hardware information, verifier definitions, preprocessing, diffusion steps, particle configurations, baseline potentials, jump lengths and stopping thresholds. It also specifies 335 Sudoku instances, 100 instances per Pixel Maze size and 100 QM9 molecules. These details were largely absent from v1.

R1.justification: V3 adds Shiryaev's Probability-1 as support for the conditional Borel–Cantelli argument in Appendix E. The existing related-work discussion, cited comparison methods and positioning relative to fixed-schedule diffusion inference remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes, MoG and Sudoku gain setup paragraphs, and the main text gains appendix cross-references. Appendices organize the additional material, but the original section order and most abstract, introduction, method, related-work, discussion and conclusion prose remain nearly verbatim.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 3–7 and Figures 9–16, including detailed comparison tables, refinement sequences, computation-allocation plots and prediction galleries. Existing main figures retain their image content, with some relocation. Figure 7's caption also changes the stated Sudoku range from 17–34 to 17–33 without changing its plot.

improvement.justification: Appendix B substantially addresses v1's sparse reproducibility information, and the added controls and diagnostics strengthen empirical support. However, Appendix E introduces a termination guarantee with material proof gaps: one optimal particle does not make the minimum top-K reward optimal (E.3), and equal rewards do not exclude nonzero-temperature particles (E.5). Because this unsupported guarantee concerns the central ATT mechanism, the documentation and empirical gains coexist with a substantive loss of theoretical reliability, leaving the overall direction uncertain.
